sections.title: I. Semantic & Valid HTML
sections.raw_content: HTML MUST be semantic and valid according to W3C standards. Use appropriate tags (`<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<nav>`, etc.) to ensure accessibility (a11y) and SEO. All images MUST have `alt` attributes, and forms MUST have associated `<label>` elements.

sections.title: II. Modular & Maintainable CSS
sections.raw_content: CSS MUST follow a modular approach (e.g., BEM naming convention) to avoid specificity wars and ensure maintainability. Use CSS Variables for colors, spacing, and typography to maintain consistency. Layouts SHOULD prioritize Flexbox and Grid for responsiveness.

sections.title: III. Clean & Modern JavaScript (ES6+)
sections.raw_content: JavaScript MUST use modern ES6+ syntax (const/let, arrow functions, destructuring, template literals). Code MUST be modular, avoiding global scope pollution. Asynchronous operations MUST be handled using `async/await` with proper `try/catch` error handling.

sections.title: IV. Separation of Concerns
sections.raw_content: Strict separation between structure (HTML), presentation (CSS), and behavior (JS) MUST be maintained. No inline styles or inline event handlers (e.g., `onclick`) are permitted.

sections.title: V. Responsive-First Design
sections.raw_content: The application MUST be fully responsive. Use a mobile-first approach with media queries to ensure a seamless experience across all device sizes.

sections.title: Project Structure
sections.raw_content:
The project MUST follow a clear and consistent directory structure:
- `/index.html`: Main entry point.
- `/css/`: All stylesheets (e.g., `style.css`, `variables.css`).
- `/js/`: All JavaScript logic, further divided into `/modules` for reusable components and `main.js` for orchestration.
- `/assets/`: Static assets such as images, icons, and fonts.

sections.title: Development Workflow
sections.raw_content:
1. **Planning**: Define the HTML structure first.
2. **Styling**: Apply CSS based on the design requirements.
3. **Behavior**: Implement JS functionality.
4. **Validation**: Validate HTML/CSS using official validators and test JS across multiple browsers.

sections.title: Governance
sections.raw_content:
This constitution serves as the primary authority for code quality and structure in the Sales Item Management project. Any deviation MUST be justified in the PR and approved by the lead developer. Amendments to this document require a version bump and a documented rationale.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-08-12 | **Last Amended**: 2026-08-12

elements.content: HTML must be semantic, W3C valid, with mandatory alt attributes for images and labels for forms.
CSS must use a modular approach (BEM), CSS Variables for consistency, and Flexbox/Grid for layouts.
JavaScript must use ES6+ syntax, be modular, and handle async operations via async/await with try/catch.
Strict separation of HTML, CSS, and JS; no inline styles or inline event handlers permitted.
Application must be fully responsive using a mobile-first approach with media queries.
Development sequence: Planning (HTML) -> Styling (CSS) -> Behavior (JS) -> Validation.
Any deviation from the constitution must be justified in the PR and approved by the lead developer.
